commands.install:
PY=$(command -v python3.13 || command -v python3.12 || command -v python3.11 || command -v python3); "$PY" -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -e '.[dev]' && cat > .venv/bin/sandbox-db <<'SANDBOX_DB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Make DATABASE_URL answer, wherever this is running. Written by the sandbox's
# install command; not part of the repo.
#
# On the runner the sandbox has already started the throwaway Postgres
# container, so the first check succeeds and this does nothing. Inside a
# role's agent container no port on the runner is reachable, so start an
# equally throwaway cluster from the PostgreSQL binaries in the image, using
# the user, password and database name DATABASE_URL already carries.
set -euo pipefail
: "${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is not set; source .factory/sandbox/.runtime.env first}"

BINDIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
PY="$BINDIR/python"

eval "$("$PY" -I -c '
import os
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

u = urlsplit(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])
print("DB_HOST=%s" % (u.hostname or "127.0.0.1"))
print("DB_PORT=%d" % (u.port or 5432))
print("DB_USER=%s" % unquote(u.username or "postgres"))
print("DB_NAME=%s" % (u.path.lstrip("/") or "postgres"))
')"

listening() {
  "$PY" -I -c '
import socket, sys
s = socket.socket()
s.settimeout(2)
sys.exit(0 if s.connect_ex((sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]))) == 0 else 1)
' "$DB_HOST" "$DB_PORT"
}

if listening; then
  echo "database: $DB_HOST:$DB_PORT already answers; using it"
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$DB_HOST" != "127.0.0.1" ] && [ "$DB_HOST" != "localhost" ]; then
  echo "database: $DB_HOST:$DB_PORT does not answer and is not local, so there is nothing to start here" >&2
  exit 1
fi

PGBIN=$(ls -d /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
if [ -z "$PGBIN" ] || [ ! -x "$PGBIN/initdb" ]; then
  PGBIN=$(dirname "$(command -v initdb 2>/dev/null || echo /nonexistent/initdb)")
fi
if [ ! -x "$PGBIN/initdb" ]; then
  echo "database: $DB_HOST:$DB_PORT does not answer, and this image has no PostgreSQL binaries to start one with" >&2
  exit 1
fi

ROOT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bsf-postgres"
DATA="$ROOT/data"
mkdir -p "$ROOT"
if [ ! -s "$DATA/PG_VERSION" ]; then
  echo "database: nothing answers on $DB_HOST:$DB_PORT, so starting a local one with $("$PGBIN/initdb" --version)"
  rm -rf "$DATA"
  "$PGBIN/initdb" -D "$DATA" -U "$DB_USER" -A trust -E UTF8 >"$ROOT/initdb.log" 2>&1 \
    || { tail -20 "$ROOT/initdb.log" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

"$PGBIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA" -l "$ROOT/server.log" -w -t 60 \
  -o "-p $DB_PORT -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 -k $ROOT -c fsync=off -c full_page_writes=off" \
  start >/dev/null 2>&1 || { tail -20 "$ROOT/server.log" >&2; exit 1; }

"$PGBIN/psql" -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$DB_PORT" -U "$DB_USER" -d postgres -tAc \
  "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '$DB_NAME'" | grep -q 1 \
  || "$PGBIN/createdb" -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$DB_PORT" -U "$DB_USER" "$DB_NAME"

echo "database: throwaway cluster up in $DATA on 127.0.0.1:$DB_PORT, database $DB_NAME"
SANDBOX_DB
chmod +x .venv/bin/sandbox-db
commands.seed:
.venv/bin/sandbox-db && .venv/bin/python -c '
from app.db import create_all, session
from app.models import Reading

create_all()
rows = [("kitchen", 21.5), ("kitchen", 19.0), ("kitchen", 23.25),
        ("garage", 8.5), ("garage", 11.0)]
with session() as db:
    for sensor, celsius in rows:
        db.add(Reading(sensor=sensor, celsius=celsius))
print("seeded %d readings across 2 sensors" % len(rows))
'

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.why: The only variable this repo reads. app/settings.py:18 is the single os.environ call in app/, and tests/conftest.py:16 is the only other one; nothing loads a .env file, which README.md states is deliberate. It names a throwaway Postgres and never anything real: the app creates its tables at startup and the test suite writes rows, so whatever this names gets written to. 127.0.0.1 is literal rather than 'localhost' as the README and ci.yml use, because localhost can resolve to ::1 where a service bound to 127.0.0.1 does not answer. Amendment round 2: 127.0.0.1:5432 means two different databases depending on where a command runs, and that is now deliberate. On the runner it is the postgres:17-alpine sidecar under services. Inside a role's agent container, which can reach no port on the runner, `.venv/bin/sandbox-db` starts an equally throwaway cluster on that address from the image's own PostgreSQL binaries. Both are worthless databases with the credentials this repo already publishes, so the address resolving locally is the point rather than a leak.

env.name: WATCHFILES_FORCE_POLLING
env.why: The app's own run configuration, needed because commands.run is now `uvicorn --reload`. The app is started by `bsf sandbox start --serve` on the runner, while the builder edits the same files from inside its container through the bind mount at /workspace. uvicorn's reloader (watchfiles) uses inotify by default; whether inotify events raised by a writer in another mount namespace reach a watcher on the runner is the one thing this setup could not test from inside a single container, and guessing wrong costs the amendment. Polling does not depend on the answer. Measured here: with polling forced, an edit to app/main.py appeared in the running app's /openapi.json 2 seconds later, over 7 files in app/.

services.name: db
services.why: The service cannot start without a database: the FastAPI lifespan in app/main.py:21-23 calls Base.metadata.create_all(), and /health runs a real SELECT 1 through a session, so it answers only when Postgres does. Seven of the eighteen tests (tests/test_api.py) need it. postgres:17-alpine is the image the repo's own compose.yaml and .github/workflows/ci.yml already use. The credentials are the repo's published throwaway ones and the container is started with --rm and no volume, so it holds nothing worth keeping. This entry also decides where roles run: bsf's needsHost() is true when a manifest has any service, which is what puts the builder and verifier on their host-access variants and lets them reach the running app on port 8787. Removing it would take that away as well as the database.

dropped.why: That is how compose makes the database throwaway. The sandbox starts the container with `docker run --rm` and no volume, which gets the same result, and the manifest's service schema has no tmpfs field to carry it.

The sandbox's only readiness option is a TCP port check (`ready: port`), and an open port is not proof the database will accept a connection. The test command makes up the difference with a real connect that retries for 60s, so an unready database fails the step rather than producing a confusing test error.

The sandbox binds the service to 127.0.0.1 only. Nothing outside the sandbox has any business reaching it — and as amendment round 2 found, nothing inside a role's agent container can reach it either, which is why `.venv/bin/sandbox-db` exists.

Compose is how a person starts the sidecar on a laptop. The sandbox starts the same postgres:17-alpine image itself from `services`, so the database is declared in one place for the factory rather than two that can drift. Docker is also not usable from inside a role's agent container, so compose could not be the fallback there.

That provisions a CI runner's interpreter; the sandbox has no Actions steps. install picks the newest interpreter already present that satisfies requires-python >= 3.11 and builds a venv from it. Measured at setup: 3.13.18.
`localhost` can resolve to ::1, where a service bound to 127.0.0.1 does not answer. The sandbox uses the literal 127.0.0.1 for both DATABASE_URL and app_url.

dropped.what: `pip install -e '.[dev]'` against the runner's system interpreter
dropped.why: setup-python makes that safe in CI. Without it, Ubuntu marks its system Python externally managed (PEP 668) and refuses the install. The sandbox uses a venv at .venv/ and calls its binaries by path, so no command depends on which interpreter is first on PATH.

exercised: All four HTTP endpoints against a real PostgreSQL: GET /health, POST /readings, GET /readings, GET /sensors/{sensor}/summary.
The whole test suite with the database present - 18 passed, including the 7 in tests/test_api.py that skip when DATABASE_URL is unset. 96% total coverage via pytest-cov.

The same 18 tests from inside a role's agent container, which is what amendment round 2 added. `.venv/bin/sandbox-db` starts a local throwaway cluster when no sidecar is reachable, so a builder gets a real database rather than 11 passed and 7 silently skipped.

A change to a route appearing in the already-running app without restarting it. commands.run is `uvicorn --reload`, so the app `bsf sandbox start --serve` left running on the runner picks up an edit made in the agent's container. Measured: a new GET /sensors route was in /openapi.json and answering 2 seconds after the file was written.
Table creation from app/models.py by Base.metadata.create_all() in the FastAPI startup lifespan.
SQLAlchemy ORM reads and writes through app/db.py's session() context manager, including its commit-on-success and rollback-on-exception path.
Pydantic validation at the edge: 422 for a reading below -273.15C or above 1000C, and for an empty sensor name.

Server-set timestamps at PostgreSQL's microsecond resolution: two consecutive POSTs to /readings get distinct recorded_at values. SQLite's second-resolution CURRENT_TIMESTAMP cannot show this, which is why the fallback is Postgres rather than a file database.
The 404 for a sensor with no readings, rather than a summary of zeros (app/summary.py:14 raising, app/main.py:72 translating).
/health as a genuine readiness check: it executes SELECT 1 through a session, so it fails when the database is gone.
ruff check . and mypy app under strict = true, the two static checks CI runs before pytest.
The rendered Swagger UI at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in a real browser - all four operations and all five schemas, captured as a full-page screenshot.

Diff and total coverage. commands.coverage runs the same 18 tests as commands.test and adds --cov-report=xml; the factory's own Cobertura reader, run here over the written coverage.xml, resolved all 7 app/ files to their repo-relative paths (app/db.py 23/26, app/main.py 42/42, app/settings.py 10/11, and so on) and 96.4% of lines overall. Before this amendment the coverage gate found no report and was neutral on every PR.

mypy as a counted static check. The declared `mypy` check writes SARIF the static gate parses: clean over app/ today (0 findings), and with two deliberate errors planted in a scratch file it produced two results with ruleIds `return-value` and `no-untyped-def` against app/_scratch_check.py, which is the per-rule-per-file shape the ratchet counts.

not_exercised.what: Schema migrations, and any change to an existing table that already holds rows.
not_exercised.why: There is no migration tool in this repo - no alembic/ directory and nothing in pyproject.toml's dependencies. The app calls Base.metadata.create_all(), which creates tables that do not exist and never alters one that does. Every database the sandbox offers starts empty, so a column change that would break a populated table passes here.

not_exercised.what: Durability: data surviving a restart, retention, or backup.
not_exercised.why: The sidecar runs from `docker run --rm` with no volume, and the in-container fallback cluster lives under TMPDIR and dies with the job. Within one job the fallback does persist across commands - it is the same cluster each time `.venv/bin/sandbox-db` is called - but nothing here can tell a change that preserves data across a deploy from one that silently discards it.

The engine's pool_pre_ping (app/db.py:19) and the module-level engine and sessionmaker singletons are only ever driven one request at a time here. Pool exhaustion, a session leaking across requests, and reconnecting after the database drops a connection are all unreached.

not_exercised.what: How the database connection is secured - TLS, sslmode, or any credential handling.
not_exercised.why: DATABASE_URL points at a throwaway Postgres over loopback with a published password and no sslmode, and the in-container fallback is initdb'd with `-A trust`, so it does not check the password at all. A change to how the connection string is built, or to what the app does when a credential is absent or wrong, has no realistic case here.

not_exercised.what: Agreement between PostgreSQL versions. A role's agent container runs the tests on a different major version than the trial does.
not_exercised.why: The sidecar is pinned to postgres:17-alpine, the image compose.yaml and ci.yml use. The fallback cluster inside an agent container is whatever the runner image ships, measured here as PostgreSQL 18.7. The suite passes on both, but version-specific SQL could pass for a builder and fail in the gates, or the reverse. What the owner actually runs is recorded nowhere in this repo, so neither number is known to be right.

not_exercised.what: The app as it would actually be served: a single non-reloading process.
not_exercised.why: commands.run is now `uvicorn --reload`, a file-watching supervisor that re-execs a worker, so that a builder's edit reaches the app already running on the runner. Nothing here exercises startup cost, a worker count above one, or any behaviour that differs between the reloader's child and a plain process. The lifespan's create_all() does run on every reload, which is harmless only because it is idempotent.

not_exercised.what: Type checking of the test suite itself, and coverage of test code.
not_exercised.why: The declared mypy check runs `mypy app`, and commands.coverage measures `--cov=app`, both following .github/workflows/ci.yml. mypy is in fact clean over `app tests` here (12 source files), but checking tests would make the static gate stricter than commands.build, so an untyped helper added to a new test is not counted. Coverage has the sharper edge: a change that touches only tests/ has no file in the report, diffCoverage returns null, and runCoverageGate reads null as 100%, so it passes the coverage gate with nothing measured.

static_checks.name: mypy
static_checks.why: mypy under `strict = true` is the second checker .github/workflows/ci.yml runs and the second half of commands.build, and bsf's runStaticTools has no native mypy, so without this entry every type error the repo already forbids is invisible to the static gate. ruff is deliberately not declared here: runStaticTools runs it natively whenever a pyproject.toml is present, so declaring it would count each ruff finding twice. mypy has no SARIF writer, so the command converts its own `--output json` lines - one JSON object per finding, each with the repo-relative file, the line and the error code - into SARIF with the venv's interpreter. The error code becomes the SARIF ruleId, which is what the gate ratchets per rule per file. The converter refuses to write a SARIF when mypy exits anything other than 0 or 1, because 2 means a crash or a bad invocation and a SARIF with no results would read as a clean repo; writing nothing makes the trial drop the check loudly instead. It writes outside the workspace so the checkout the gate also diffs stays clean. `mypy app` rather than `mypy app tests` matches ci.yml and commands.build, so the static gate never disagrees with the build a builder can run.
